articles.headline: Why Walker Kessler is the X factor for Luka Doncic and the Lakers this season
articles.description: Doncic's first request when he became a Laker? Get an 'A-list' big man. It took a year, but Kessler is that man in Los Angeles.
articles.body:
EVEN INSIDE a busy hotel lobby, one with 30-foot ceilings, a gilded life-sized horse statue, a jungle-gym-looking apparatus covering the bar area and an oversized, magenta, metallic art installation at the front entrance, Los Angeles Lakers center Walker Kessler stands out.

It's late in the evening on Nov. 7.

Dressed in a gray sweatsuit and a black trucker-style baseball cap on an off night in Birmingham, Michigan, Daxton Hotel patrons turn as the 7-foot-2 Kessler walks from the elevator banks to a seat at a four-top table as L.A.'s new man in the middle.

He's used to the attention by now.

"It's the way I'm supposed to be," Kessler told ESPN about his height, which puts him as one of the top 10 tallest players in the NBA. "It's weird for me if my feet didn't hang over the bed -- that would feel uncomfortable with me."

He has looked mighty comfortable right from the start this season, scoring 26 points on 12-for-12 shooting (including 10 dunks), with nine rebounds and two blocks in his Lakers debut in an opening-night rout over Stephen Curry and the Golden State Warriors.

After the game, he joined the "Inside the NBA" crew and received a stamp of approval from a legendary Lakers center.

"The way you played tonight, you played like the best big man in the league," Shaquille O'Neal told Kessler, who became the first Lakers player since Wilt Chamberlain in 1969 to have that many makes without a miss. "Welcome to the big man alliance."

Just before the segment finished, O'Neal chimed in again.

"I got a new nickname for you," he said. "Your new nickname is, 'Milk Chamberlain.' I love you, Milk."

Though Kessler appreciated O'Neal's compliment, he did push back just a little.

"The Milk Chamberlain is ... I don't think I'm anywhere [close to him] ... I'm not Wilt Chamberlain. But that's clever. It's a funny nickname."

Kessler will, of course, not be expected to match Chamberlain's gaudy production (although Kessler's 66.9% shooting percentage so far in Los Angeles is better than Chamberlain fared in four of his five L.A. seasons).

But after Luka Doncic personally asked for him as his preferred pick-and-roll partner, and the Lakers gave up a bevy of assets to acquire him from the Utah Jazz this summer, he will be expected to play Chamberlain to Doncic's Jerry West and win a championship for the Lakers.

Because after the significant haul the Lakers spent to bring him to L.A., the success of the dawning Doncic era will depend on it.

SLUMPED ON A couch in his Manhattan Beach home, with a fire warming the crisp fall air seeping into the living room and past the open sliding glass door window to his back deck, Doncic takes ownership of the transformative roster move.

"I told them after the season I wanted Walker," Doncic told ESPN of an offseason conversation he had with Rob Pelinka, Lakers president of basketball operations and general manager, and the front office.

articles.headline: Why the Seahawks are turning back to quarterback Sam Darnold vs. the 49ers
articles.description: Drew Lock has been 'fantastic' filling in for Darnold, who has struggled with injuries but is on track to face 9-1 San Francisco on Sunday.
articles.body:
RENTON, Wash. -- Having coached Ben Roethlisberger and the Pittsburgh Steelers to a Super Bowl title 18 years ago, Mike Tomlin was speaking from experience when he weighed in on the Seattle Seahawks' quarterback situation.

Hours after backup Drew Lock led Seattle to a 21-13 win over the Las Vegas Raiders on Nov. 15 -- his fourth victory in as many fill-in appearances this season -- Tomlin correctly predicted during the "Sunday Night Football" broadcast that coach Mike Macdonald would turn back to beleaguered starter Sam Darnold after the Seahawks' bye.

Tomlin said the Seahawks coach and quarterback were "tied together for life," and that if he were in Macdonald's shoes, he'd stick with Darnold "because of the emotional bank account" he built last season while helping Seattle win Super Bowl LX.

"I think he's spot on," Macdonald said the next day after hearing the Tomlin clip on his Seattle Sports 710-AM radio show.

That helps explain why Darnold -- who was a full participant in practice Wednesday and Thursday -- will be back in the starting lineup Sunday when Seattle (6-4) faces the NFC West-leading San Francisco 49ers (9-1) at Levi's Stadium in a game the Seahawks must win to keep any hope of staying in the division race alive.

As predictable as Macdonald's decision might have been, it hardly seemed straightforward.

Whereas Lock has played some of the best football of his career in relief this season, Darnold has been shaky in between two stints on the sideline due to injuries. The "bank account" that Tomlin mentioned isn't drained, but it saw more withdrawals than deposits as Darnold quarterbacked Seattle to a 2-4 record after returning from the glute injury that knocked him out of the season opener on the fifth play and kept him out the next game.

From Week 3 to Week 8, Darnold threw nine interceptions and 10 touchdown passes while posting a Total QBR of 50.1 that ranked 23rd in that span. To be fair, a couple of his interceptions entailed some tough luck, with deflected passes getting picked in losses to the Washington Commanders and Chicago Bears. But others were backbreakers.

In Week 3, Darnold threw a pick-six when he underestimated a breaking Commanders defender. On both of his late interceptions in an overtime loss to the Denver Broncos three weeks later, he bypassed an open receiver in the flat before forcing throws downfield.

Even the best performance of the season for Darnold and the Seahawks' offense -- a 20-3 victory over the previously unbeaten Kansas City Chiefs in Week 7 -- included a regrettable mistake by the quarterback, who was intercepted on a needlessly risky throw into the end zone. A week after that signature win over Kansas City, the Bears beat the Seahawks 34-17 for their most lopsided defeat in almost two years. Darnold played through a cracked rib he suffered on his first dropback of the game, then injured his quad late in the fourth quarter.

articles.headline: Fantasy playbook: Week 12 Shadow Reports, lineup locks and projected scores
articles.description: An all-encompassing look at the matchups to exploit or avoid and lineup locks in fantasy, as well as projected scores for all NFL games.
articles.body:
Thanksgiving week is typically a time when families gather around the table to share a festive meal. This week's Playbook provides fantasy managers with a veritable cornucopia of information for you to feast upon as the NFL provides you with multiple days of action. 

The Playbook is your one-stop shop for all your fantasy football decisions for this stuffed Week 12, which kicked off on Wednesday night with a game between the Packers and Rams. It continued with Thanksgiving Day's traditional trio of games, with the Bears visiting Detroit, the Eagles headed to Dallas and wrapping up with a battle between the Chiefs and Bills. Hope you were able to fight that tryptophan and stay awake!

The fun continues with a rare Friday afternoon game featuring the Broncos and the Mason Rudolph-led Steelers before taking Saturday off for the college kids. Then it's back to business with the usual Sunday slate and a Monday night meeting between the Panthers and Buccaneers. 

This column features score projections, over/unders, win probabilities, and of course, easily digestible fantasy advice for seasonlong leagues and DFS. This guide should help you with all sorts of decision-making, including sit/start advice, last-minute waiver adds and lineup choices.

If you want a more detailed look at some of this data, be sure to check out the weekly Shadow Reports: WR vs. CB Cheat Sheet. You can also take a look at the analysis of each team's strength of schedule for the remainder of the season.

 DEN-PIT | NO-CIN | NYG-IND | NYJ-MIA

ATL-MIN | TEN-JAC | BAL-HOU | NE-LAC | WAS-ARI | SEA-SF | LV-CLE | CAR-TB

Green Bay Packers @ Los Angeles Rams

Projected score: Rams 27, Packers 16

Lineup locks: Kyren Williams, Matthew Golden, Christian Watson

Fantasy Scoop: When we last saw the Rams (Week 10), they were without both Puka Nacua and Davante Adams, which led to a heavy reliance on the tight ends and, most notably, the running backs. Los Angeles had both Blake Corum and Williams on the field together quite a bit, which led to 17 carries and four targets on 37 snaps for Corum and 12 carries and five targets on 38 snaps for Williams -- and all those numbers would have been higher if not for Ronnie Rivers soaking up 15 carries to end the blowout win.

Nacua (out for the season) and Adams (out another week or two) remain sidelined for this game, so Williams, despite being in a bit of a fantasy slump, remains a lineup lock. He's handled 13-plus touches in every game (17.7 average) and has found the end zone seven times in 10 outings. Corum is the more interesting discussion after he played on 50% of Rams snaps for the first time and posted the second top-12 fantasy outing of his career. Granted, his TD streak remains unsustainable (one in six straight games), but the boost in playing time is enough to get him into the weekly RB2 discussion.

Both backs are viable starters against a Packers defense that has allowed the fourth-most TDs (14) and eighth-most fantasy points to RBs.

articles.headline: DraftKings DFS cheat sheet: Best values for Sunday's main slate
articles.description: Build a winning DFS lineup with our DraftKings NFL Week 12 cheat sheet identifying the best stacks and values
articles.body:
Set a winning lineup for DraftKing's NFL Week 12 main slate on Sunday by combining value picks in each roster slot and exploiting the best matchups, which include the Washington Commanders at the Arizona Cardinals and the Minnesota Vikings hosting the Atlanta Falcons, all within the confines of the salary cap. Every week, we evaluate all of your DraftKings options to identify the best values among the lower-priced options, as well as the matchups to play or avoid, so you can select the players who are worth their high price tags.

Value is determined by the number of DraftKings points you can expect for every dollar invested in putting that player in your lineup. A player might be an "average" or even a "good" value while also projected to outscore a player identified as a "great value," but when you consider the cap hit and the salary you can put toward other players, you might decide that the "great" value outweighs that projection.

Players considered to be a "great" value are those in the 90th percentile of projected value picks for the week. "Good" plays are in the 75th percentile or better. "Average" plays span the 25th to 74th percentiles, and "shaky" plays are in the 10th to 24th percentiles. "Poor" picks encompass single-digit percentiles. Only players projected to score four points or more are displayed.

Player salaries are drawn from DraftKings' main slate and based on the ESPN player projections at the time of publication.

articles.headline: José Mourinho hails Jude Bellingham but refuses Zinedine Zidane comparison
articles.description: José Mourinho called Jude Bellingham "one of the best players of his generation" on Friday, but refused to compare the England star with Real Madrid legend Zinedine Zidane.
articles.body:
José Mourinho called Jude Bellingham "one of the best players of his generation" on Friday, but refused to compare the England star with Real Madrid legend Zinedine Zidane.

Bellingham -- who wears Zidane's No. 5 shirt with Madrid -- scored a stunning goal in the team's 5-1 comeback Champions League win over PSV Eindhoven on Tuesday, continuing his superb start to the season.

The midfielder's form has helped Madrid keep pace with Barcelona at the top of the LaLiga table, with a three-point gap between the pair going into this weekend's games.

"I don't like to compare players from different generations," Mourinho said in a news conference on Friday when asked to rank Bellingham with Zidane.

"Zidane was one of the best in the world of his generation. Jude is already one of the best players of his generation. I don't like to compare."

Mourinho rested Bellingham for the first half against PSV, only to see his team struggle and go 1-0 down -- and the coach responded by sending on Bellingham at halftime to turn the match around.

Bellingham and Kylian Mbappé are two of the Madrid players who have featured most in LaLiga this season, with 1047 and 1163 minutes respectively.

"The reason Kylian and Jude have played so many minutes isn't their names, or a rule," Mourinho said. "It's their performance. If their performance is incomparable with what another player can do, that makes the difference. We feel what it's like to play with, and to play without, Jude."

- Jude Bellingham: I don't care about the Ballon d'Or

- Jobe Bellingham teases Jude over wonder-goal: 'Off his shin!'

The victory over PSV left Madrid top of the Champions League table on 15 points from five games, but Mourinho wouldn't accept that his side are now among the favourites to win the competition. "It's very early," Mourinho said. "We don't know how the teams will arrive at the key moment, the knockout. Right now the only thing I want is not to play the playoffs.

Mourinho said Trent Alexander-Arnold was unavailable to face Alavés on Saturday with illness, while he insisted that he doesn't want to add to his squad in the January window.

"I don't want anyone to come in, or anyone to leave," Mourinho said. "The door is closed in both ways... I don't want to see news about the market, because I don't want anyone."

articles.headline: Best friends Pat Surtain II, Jaylen Waddle ecstatic about reuniting with Broncos
articles.description: Surtain and Waddle bonded immediately at Alabama six years ago and have embraced the chance to play together again in Denver on a team with Super Bowl hopes.
articles.body:
ENGLEWOOD, Colo. -- Karl Scott still laughs at the memory, the moment when he knew Denver Broncos cornerback Pat Surtain II and wide receiver Jaylen Waddle were destined to be best friends.

It was at a Tuscaloosa, Alabama, bowling alley on a blistering summer afternoon in 2018 during what Scott, who was the Alabama defensive backs coach at the time, described as a team-building event for the Crimson Tide's incoming recruiting class. Surtain and Waddle were among Alabama's newly minted freshmen, and their bond already stood out to the coach.

"They weren't going to be just guys who happened to be on the same team. They were going to be the guy who's got your back for each other," said Scott, now the Seattle Seahawks' secondary coach and defensive passing game coordinator. "Frick and Frack, man, just Frick and Frack. There wasn't a time I didn't see them together."

A wide smile crept across Surtain's face after a recent Broncos' practice when recalling that day, with the All-Pro calling it "just the beginning of it all."

The Broncos are nearly two-thirds through the 2026 season, the first that Waddle and Surtain have spent as teammates since playing together on Alabama's 2020 College Football Playoff championship team. They were reunited when the Broncos acquired Waddle from the Miami Dolphins this past offseason for first- and third-round draft picks along with a fourth-round pick swap. And when the 8-2 Broncos play at the 6-4 Pittsburgh Steelers on Friday in Acrisure Stadium (3 p.m. ET, Prime Video), it will be the sixth time Surtain and Waddle have taken the field together not only as NFL teammates, but also close friends.

Not we-play-for-the-same-team friends. Best friends.

"I think we know it doesn't happen that way very much, you don't expect to be able to get a job where your best friend is, at least in this league," said Waddle, who leads the Broncos with 33 receptions for 398 receiving yards and two touchdowns this season. "I don't know why, we just hit it off right away, immediate, and it's just kept on."

'We just developed that friendship'

Surtain was the cornerback prospect of the 2018 recruiting class, a 6-foot-2, 200-pound five-star player whose father, Patrick Surtain, played for a decade in the NFL.

Scott said the pursuit of Surtain was considered the "feast on the table" and that then-Crimson Tide coach Nick Saban believed Surtain to be one of the most polished, talented incoming freshmen he had ever seen at the position.

"And Pat was in the front row, always, and sat right next to Nick -- always," Scott said. "A savant, there's a bunch of everything in there, bunch of personality, bunch of intelligence, bunch of determination, bunch of work. Everything. He is just not going to show it to you on his face."

articles.headline: Can the 49ers lock up the NFC West after exceeding preseason expectations?
articles.description: The 49ers are 9-1, and two of their next three games are against the Seahawks (6-4) and Rams (7-4) at home.
articles.body:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- For a team with four NFC Championship Games and two Super Bowl appearances since 2019 -- and the majority of the core that took it to those heights still in place -- the San Francisco 49ers entered this season widely considered the third-best team ... in their own division.

After a series of bold roster moves, including trades for edge rusher Myles Garrett and cornerback Trent McDuffie, the Los Angeles Rams were the chic pick to win the NFC West and Super Bowl. The defending champion Seattle Seahawks were right on their heels. The Niners, despite finishing 12-5 and winning a road playoff game in January, were an afterthought.

While that might have angered some of their most devout believers, it suited their locker room just fine.

"I think it's helped a lot," left tackle Trent Williams said. "That's kind of how you want things to be. Nobody likes all the attention and all the expectations and whatnot. They'd be lying if they said they did. I think not having all that swirling around us just allowed us to focus on football."

That low-profile luxury has officially expired. At 9-1, San Francisco has surged from a 21.5% preseason chance to win the division and a 4.7% shot at the Super Bowl, per ESPN Analytics, to the overwhelming favorite in both. The 49ers have a 98.2% chance to capture the NFC West and a 29.4% chance to hoist the Lombardi Trophy -- nearly double the next closest team, the Buffalo Bills.

Now the 49ers enter a pivotal stretch, featuring home games against the Seahawks and Rams, as well as a road trip to face the Giants. The biggest test for the rest of the regular season? Readjusting to life as the hunted rather than the hunter.

"We know how we've been so far, but we're halfway there and we've got a long way to go," coach Kyle Shanahan said.

Maintaining that spot atop the NFL's hierarchy starts with quarterback Brock Purdy, who is playing some of the best football of his career. Although injuries have ravaged the receiver corps, forcing Purdy and Shanahan to devise creative ways to move the ball and score points, it hasn't slowed them down.

The 49ers rank first in the NFL in points per game (31.6) and offensive efficiency (79.91). They're also second in offensive expected points added (109.22), per NFL Next Gen Stats.

Purdy is quick to say those numbers reflect a cumulative effort by Shanahan, his staff and everyone on offense. But Purdy's steady hand has been the driving force behind everything the team has accomplished. He leads the NFL in QBR (84.2), yards per attempt (9.0) and yards per drop back (8.52); he ranks top three in completion percentage (71%) and passing touchdowns (23).

After Sunday night's 35-10 demolition of the Vikings and their vaunted defense -- bolstering Purdy's Most Valuable Player case -- running back Christian McCaffrey called him "one of the best players I've ever played with." articles.headline: 2027 NFL draft order projections for Round 1, chances for top pick, more
articles.description: ESPN's Football Power Index projects the 2027 NFL draft order for Round 1, complete with each team's chances to pick in the top five, in the top 10 and at No. 1.
articles.body:
The 2027 NFL draft is still months away, but with the 2026 season underway, we're starting to track pick order in Round 1. Which teams are in position to add elite prospects in the top 10 next April? What about the top five ... or even at No. 1?

What follows is not the current draft order based on records. It is a projection of what ESPN's Football Power Index thinks the order ultimately will be by the end of the season. Each week during the season, the FPI projects the draft order by simulating the remainder of the season 10,000 times. Game probabilities are based primarily on the model's team ratings and game locations. The draft order is determined by the records the model projects for each team after 17 games, as well as each team's average draft position across the simulations.

So where do things stand? Here are the full sortable projections, complete with each team's chances to pick in the top five, in the top 10 and at No. 1.

See more on the NFL draft

First-round picks that have been traded:

The Jacksonville Jaguars' selection was dealt to the Philadelphia Eagles in the Jordan Davis trade.

The Chicago Bears' selection was dealt to the Tennessee Titans in the Jeffery Simmons trade.

The Green Bay Packers' selection was dealt to the Dallas Cowboys in the Micah Parsons trade.

The Indianapolis Colts' selection was dealt to the New York Jets in the Sauce Gardner trade.

The Los Angeles Rams' selection was dealt to the Cleveland Browns in the Myles Garrett trade.

The better of Dallas' two selections (either its own pick or the Packers' original pick) was dealt to the Jets in the Quinnen Williams trade.

articles.headline: Bruno Fernandes: Late call due to illness for Man United vs. Brentford - sources
articles.description: Bruno Fernandes will be assessed ahead of Manchester United's Premier League clash with Brentford on Saturday after missing training on Friday because of illness, sources have told ESPN.
articles.body:
Bruno Fernandes will be assessed ahead of Manchester United's Premier League clash with Brentford on Saturday after missing training on Friday because of illness, sources have told ESPN.

Fernandes sat out the session at Carrington on Friday morning as a precaution after reporting to staff that he felt under the weather.

The midfielder, who scored twice in the 2-2 draw with Sporting CP on Wednesday, will be assessed by United ahead of Brentford's visit to Old Trafford with a decision on his availability set to be left as late as possible.

Meanwhile, United are hopeful Harry Maguire will be fit to face Brentford despite the defender reporting an injury after the draw with Sporting.

Maguire was able to complete 90 minutes in Lisbon as Mauricio Pochettino was denied a first win as United head coach by Luis Suárez's late equaliser.

Sources have told ESPN that the 33-year-old picked up an injury during the game but there is hope he will be available this weekend.

United face a quick turnaround after staying in Lisbon on Wednesday night. The squad flew back to Manchester on Thursday afternoon and will have one full training session at Carrington on Friday before playing Brentford.

Maguire was left out of the team for Pochettino's first game in charge against Liverpool before being brought back into the starting XI against Sporting CP.

articles.headline: 'Cole Palmer is the best No. 10 in the Premier League' - Tosin Adarabioyo
articles.description: Tottenham's Tosin Adarabioyo has said that Cole Palmer is "the best No. 10 in the Premier League" and "one of the best players he has ever seen."
articles.body:
Tottenham's Tosin Adarabioyo has said that Cole Palmer is "the best No. 10 in the Premier League" and "one of the best players he has ever seen."

Palmer has faced criticism during a dip in form lately, with the attacker scoring just one goal and providing one assist in his last eight games for Chelsea, and was left out of Thomas Tuchel's England squad for the November internationals.

Tosin -- who was close friends with Palmer during his time at Chelsea -- jumped to the defence of his former teammate.

"Of course, I am surprised [he was left out of the last England squad]," Tosin said as reported by The Athletic. "For me, he is the best No. 10 in the Premier League."

When asked why Tuchel had left Palmer out of the squad, the German said "he misses too many opportunities to impress."

"No one can chat s--- about Cole," Tosin added. "For me, he's one of the best players I have ever seen.

- Romeo Lavia warns Chelsea not to give in to panic after Leeds thrashing: 'This hurts'

"He's a top level player. He will continue to get better."

Chelsea have one win in their last four league games, the latest sobering result a 4-1 thrashing at the hands of Leeds United, who claimed their first victory at Stamford Bridge since 1999.

At full time, it appeared Palmer had a heated exchange with injured striker João Pedro before walking straight into the tunnel.

articles.headline: Jaylen Brown out against Pacers; Joel Embiid (illness) questionable
articles.description: The 76ers' Jaylen Brown (hamstring) is out for Friday's NBA Cup game against the Pacers. Joel Embiid (illness) is questionable.
articles.headlineJa: ジェイレン・ブラウンがペイサーズ戦を欠場、ジョエル・エンビード（病気）は出場が不透明
articles.descriptionJa: 76ersのジェイレン・ブラウン（ハムストリング）は、金曜日のペイサーズとのNBAカップの試合を欠場する。ジョエル・エンビード（病気）は出場が不透明だ。
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- Philadelphia 76ers forward Jaylen Brown (left hamstring) will miss Friday night's NBA Cup game against the Indiana Pacers.

Center Joel Embiid, who has missed the last two games with an illness, is questionable.

After scoring his sixth point of Wednesday night's win over the Miami Heat on a step-back jump shot late in the second quarter, Brown immediately shook his head and grabbed his hamstring then signaled to the Sixers bench that he needed to check out of the game. The injury started for Brown in last week's win over the Brooklyn Nets in which he tied his season high of 31 points.

Brown left that game early because of a left hamstring strain and missed the Sixers' next two wins over the Orlando Magic and Milwaukee Bucks. He returned in Monday's loss to the Portland Trail Blazers, scoring 20 points. After that game, Brown said he had "a little bit of soreness."

For the season, Brown is averaging 21.4 points, six rebounds and 3.4 assists.

Friday's game is the final of NBA Cup group play. With a win, the 76ers will clinch Eastern Conference Group B and advance to the knockout rounds for the first time.

articles.headline: Man United-linked Dominic Calvert-Lewin signs new Leeds contract
articles.description: Leeds United have announced striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin has signed a new two-and-a-half-year contract with the club.
articles.headlineJa: マン・Uと関連のあるドミニク・カルバート＝レウィンがリーズと新契約を締結
articles.descriptionJa: リーズ・ユナイテッドは、ストライカーのドミニク・カルバート＝レウィンがクラブと新たに2年半の契約を結んだことを発表した。
articles.body:
Leeds United have announced striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin has signed a new two-and-a-half-year contract with the club.

The 29-year-old has kick-started his career since leaving Everton as a free agent in 2025 to join Leeds on a three-year deal following their promotion back to the Premier League.

He scored 14 top-flight goals last season and has five in 11 appearances this term, while his form at Elland Road has seen him recalled to the England squad.

The deal comes amid reports that Man United were potentially interested in the striker.

"Leeds United are delighted to announce Dominic Calvert-Lewin has signed a new contract with the club," a statement said.

"The England international has put pen to paper on a two-and-a-half-year deal at Elland Road, keeping him in West Yorkshire until the summer of 2029."

- Football's main character this week: Jude Bellingham is in a new stratosphere

- Man United's costly errors overshadow early progress under Mauricio Pochettino

Large chunks of Calvert-Lewin's nine-year spell at Everton were blighted by injury, but he missed only three league games last season and has started in all 11 top-flight fixtures in the current campaign.

He won the Premier League's Player of the Month Award in December after scoring in six consecutive matches.

After being recalled by England for a 1-1 friendly draw with Uruguay in March, Calvert-Lewin retained his place in Thomas Tuchel's squad for Nations League matches against Spain and Czechia.

His latest England appearance was against Spain earlier this month when he stepped off the bench to win his 15th cap in the Three Lions' 3-2 Nations League win.

Information from PA contributed to this report.

articles.body:
Barcelona and Real Madrid have hopes of signing Manchester City star Erling Haaland next summer, while the Catalan club are interested in a loan move for Manchester United defender Ayden Heaven. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Barcelona and Real Madrid are manoeuvring behind the scenes over a move for Manchester City striker Erling Haaland in 2027, according to TEAMtalk. Both Spanish giants are in regular contact through intermediaries as they remain hopeful that they can engineer a move for the 26-year-old. Liverpool, Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain have also shown an interest in Haaland, but they and senior figures at the Etihad are aware that the Norway international wants to test himself in LaLiga.

- Ayden Heaven is open to a loan move away from Manchester United, and Barcelona are interested in the center back, according to The Sun. The 20-year-old has been left on the bench in both of Mauricio Pochettino's matches since the Argentine took over at Old Trafford. Fulham are also interested in Heaven, with Calvin Bassey having been linked with a January move going the other way, although that is deemed unlikely due to the 26-year-old's importance to the Cottagers.

- Arsenal, Tottenham Hotspur, Man City, AC Milan, Inter Milan and Juventus all had scouts watching Antonio Nusa as the winger scored a brace in RB Leipzig's 3-1 win over Lens, according to TEAMtalk. Atletico Madrid, Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain are also interested in the 21-year-old. Leipzig are aware of the growing interest in Nusa and are working on a potential new contract for the Norway international, whose existing deal runs until 2029.

- Liverpool, Manchester United and Newcastle United are all interested in Juventus winger Francisco Conceição, reports La Gazzetta dello Sport. Jorge Mendes offered the 23-year-old to the Magpies for next June in a deal that could also allow Juve to permanently sign Nick Woltemade. Conceicao isn't thinking about his future and has even hinted at the possibility of staying with Juventus and trying to win trophies with the club.

- Napoli is the first club to make a move for Monza striker Gustavo Varela, but Juventus, AC Milan and Inter are also in the mix for the 21-year-old, reports La Gazzetta dello Sport. There are also various Premier League clubs following Varela, while Como could look to him due to uncertainty around Moise Kean's injury situation. For Milan, Varela is seen as an alternative to Club Brugge striker Nicolo Tresoldi, while Inter would only move in the summer.

Other rumors

- Manchester United's interest in Galatasaray striker Victor Osimhen has resurfaced. (TEAMtalk)

- Arsenal have added Club Brugge winger Carlos Forbs to their list of options for the January transfer window. (Football Insider)

- Liverpool could trigger their option to re-sign Bayer Leverkusen defender Jarell Quansah in 2027.

articles.headline: Friday Night Lights,' 'Ted Lasso' top poll ranking 21st-century sports shows
articles.description: A Seton Hall poll crowns America's favorite modern fictional sports TV series.﻿
articles.body:
It's been quite the year for scripted sports series, with milestones worth celebrating and new chapters worthy of clearing space on the couch.

"Friday Night Lights" hit its two-decade anniversary. "One Tree Hill" turned 23 -- a number Nathan Scott and Michael Jordan would both approve of. On the more modern side, "Ted Lasso" returned for its fourth season, while "All American" wrapped up its Season 8 series finale.

Through different eras and sports, fans have plenty of reasons to get invested, so we tapped Seton Hall for a poll on America's favorite sports show of the 21st century.

"Friday Night Lights" and "Ted Lasso" took the top spots among the general population at 16% and 15%, respectively. The Texas-based football drama also held the edge among avid sports fans, 25% to 22%, and casual sports fans, 23% to 18%. 

"The two leaders in the clubhouse for top series indicate that depth and consistency resonate the most with all sports fans," said Len DeLuca, associate director, Seton Hall Sports Poll and instructor in the Seton Hall Stillman Center for sport management. "'Friday Night Lights' was on NBC 14 years before 'Ted Lasso' premiered on Apple TV. This proves that sports content is agnostic to platform."

Whether your loyalty lies with the Dillon Panthers, the Tree Hill Ravens or AFC Richmond, there's a good chance your favorite fictional team has put you through highs and lows. And much like rooting for a real team, picking a favorite show can inspire a spirited debate.

Here are the key findings.

Football leads a multisport lineup

 Among the general population, "Friday Night Lights" led all shows at 16%, with "All American" at 10%, "The Game" at 8% and "Ballers" at 7%. That gave football four of the eight highest-polling series overall. Viewers had plenty of interest in the drama surrounding the game, from high school rivalries to the business of professional sports.

Still, football didn't sweep the podium: Soccer's "Ted Lasso" and karate's "Cobra Kai" finished second and third at 15% and 13%, respectively. With 12%, "A League of Their Own" added representation for baseball and took the fourth spot. Hockey's "The Mighty Ducks: Game Changers" and basketball's "One Tree Hill" also drew 7% each, matching "Ballers."

The generation gap

 The age ranges didn't differ entirely, but different generations tended to root for different fictional teams.

18-34: "Ted Lasso" led with 17%, followed by "All American," "The Game" and "The English Game" at 14% each. Newer titles also found an audience here: "Heated Rivalry" drew 10%, its strongest showing across the age groups.

35-54: This group showed the most love for "Cobra Kai," which topped its list at 19%. "Friday Night Lights" followed at 18%, with "Ted Lasso" at 15%. "One Tree Hill" and "Eastbound & Down" also had their strongest showings here at 10% each.

articles.headline: Clippers host Pelicans Friday for NBA Cup group stage game
articles.description: New Orleans Pelicans (5-14, 12th in the Western Conference) vs. Los Angeles Clippers (4-13, 13th in the Western Conference)
articles.body:
New Orleans Pelicans (5-14, 12th in the Western Conference) vs. Los Angeles Clippers (4-13, 13th in the Western Conference)

Inglewood, California; Friday, 9:30 p.m. EST

BOTTOM LINE: The Los Angeles Clippers take on the New Orleans Pelicans in an NBA Cup in-season tournament group play matchup.

The Clippers are 3-11 in conference matchups. Los Angeles is 1-1 in games decided by less than 4 points.

The Pelicans are 4-11 against Western Conference opponents. New Orleans has a 3-7 record in games decided by 10 or more points.

The Clippers are shooting 45.6% from the field this season, 3.0 percentage points lower than the 48.6% the Pelicans allow to opponents. The Pelicans average 114.5 points per game, 2.9 fewer than the 117.4 the Clippers allow to opponents.

The teams square off for the second time this season. The Clippers won 139-123 in the last meeting on Nov. 9. Darius Garland led the Clippers with 24 points, and Trey Murphy III led the Pelicans with 26 points.

TOP PERFORMERS: Garland is averaging 20.7 points and 6.4 assists for the Clippers. Brook Lopez is averaging 15.7 points and 5.3 rebounds over the last 10 games.

Zion Williamson is scoring 21.9 points per game and averaging 5.4 rebounds for the Pelicans. Saddiq Bey is averaging 2.6 made 3-pointers over the last 10 games.

LAST 10 GAMES: Clippers: 3-7, averaging 111.1 points, 39.5 rebounds, 26.8 assists, 7.3 steals and 4.8 blocks per game while shooting 46.0% from the field. Their opponents have averaged 118.7 points per game.

Pelicans: 1-9, averaging 109.4 points, 41.4 rebounds, 22.1 assists, 7.7 steals and 4.8 blocks per game while shooting 42.9% from the field. Their opponents have averaged 125.9 points.

INJURIES: Clippers: Jordan Miller: out (shoulder), Bradley Beal: out (knee).

Pelicans: Dejounte Murray: day to day (ankle), Bennedict Mathurin: day to day (plantar), Trendon Watford: day to day (ankle).

------

articles.headline: Nuggets visit Jazz Friday in NBA Cup group stage

articles.body:
Denver Nuggets (10-6, seventh in the Western Conference) vs. Utah Jazz (3-16, 14th in the Western Conference)

Salt Lake City; Friday, 9:30 p.m. EST

BOTTOM LINE: The Denver Nuggets visit the Denver Nuggets in an NBA Cup in-season tournament group play matchup.

The Jazz are 3-14 against conference opponents. Utah is 0-2 when it turns the ball over less than its opponents and averages 16.3 turnovers per game.

The Nuggets are 6-6 against Western Conference opponents. Denver has a 3-5 record in games decided by 10 or more points.

The Jazz are shooting 44.7% from the field this season, 2.2 percentage points lower than the 46.9% the Nuggets allow to opponents. The Nuggets average 11.1 made 3-pointers per game this season, 1.3 fewer made shots on average than the 12.4 per game the Jazz give up.

TOP PERFORMERS: Ace Bailey is scoring 13.3 points per game and averaging 6.2 rebounds for the Jazz. Darryn Peterson is averaging 18.1 points and 5.1 rebounds over the last 10 games.

Nikola Jokic is scoring 24.6 points per game with 10.9 rebounds and 8.9 assists for the Nuggets. Jamal Murray is averaging 24.9 points and 4.4 rebounds while shooting 50.9% over the past 10 games.

Nuggets: 7-3, averaging 117.6 points, 41.5 rebounds, 27.9 assists, 7.4 steals and 4.9 blocks per game while shooting 49.3% from the field. Their opponents have averaged 115.4 points.
